newsitem.title: GERMANY: Shrempp - Daimler recovery well underway.
newsitem.headline: Shrempp - Daimler recovery well underway.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG chief executive Juergen Schrempp said on Wednesday the German industrial group's recovery after a record 5.7 billion mark loss in 1995 was well underway but not yet completed.
"These decisions are beginning to pay off earlier and more markedly than many expected," Schrempp said of the 1996 results in a statement issued by Daimler at its annual news conference.
"Our productivity and efficieny initiatives are showing their initial success," he said.
But he added: "We also recognise that Daimler-Benz has only completed the first step on the road toward becoming one of the world's leading corporations."

Daimler reported a 1996 operating profit according to U.S. GAAP accounting rules of 2.42 billion marks following an operating loss in 1995 of 7.20 billion marks as Schrempp started the largest corporate restructuring in German history.

"A year ago I presented tough but necessary measures to you that were intended to bring Daimler-Benz back up to a first-class earnings level. And I promised our return to profit. We accomplished this first step. Today we can say: This result confirms our strategy," Schrempp said in the statement.

Schrempp said Daimler's decisions to shed itself of loss-making units, such as its AEG electronics group and troubled Dutch aircraft maker Fokker, as part of the restructuring were "paying off" and were evident in Daimler's return to profitability in 1996.
Schrempp said Daimler's business areas, which also include the Mercedes passenger car and commercial truck division, were positioned in high-growth international markets
